nextChange: Balanced postings through public ledger package, preserving native Python journey and standards; recommendations only.

sources.summary: Public package, ledger ownership and balanced postings using native Python checks.
Ledger owns entries and paired posting; amount quantizes using ambient Decimal context.
Limited scan and exact app import matching; alternate private imports pass disposable fixtures.
Only happy posting and negative posting covered.
Native Python CLI exports CSV stdout and JSON file successfully.
Posting and balance operations form one cohesive domain owner; splitting is not justified.

findings.principle: External modules use the public ledger package.
findings.consequence: Caller depends on private normalization already owned by post().
findings.fix: Remove private import and pass string 10 directly to Ledger.post; retain from ledger import Ledger. Do not expose amount or add a bridge.
findings.verification: opening_balance remains Decimal(10.00); boundary check passes; CLI rows unchanged.

findings.problem: Boundary checker misses from ledger import _internal and allows from ledger.book import Ledger; startup and future external modules are not scanned.
findings.principle: Enforce public package access across all external callers.
findings.consequence: Native check can be green while callers bypass the public API. find_spec can execute parent package code, so analysis is not purely static.
findings.fix: Extend existing AST checker to discover repository Python consumers, resolve from-import members, aliases, package entry points and internal relative imports statically. Keep internal ledger imports allowed; avoid a forwarding facade.
findings.verification: Disposable valid public/internal fixtures pass; direct private, from-import private, aliases and external book imports fail. Cover new/nested caller, relative resolution and cycles; unsupported dynamic imports are explicit limitations.

findings.problem: post accepts NaN when caller disables InvalidOperation trap and balanced() becomes False.
findings.principle: All successful postings preserve finite balanced entries.
findings.consequence: Ambient caller Decimal settings can invalidate ledger state.
findings.fix: Reject non-finite amounts explicitly before comparisons and mutation at shared normalization boundary. Keep two-decimal normalization and atomic import staging; define consistent public invalid-value errors. No exception permitting non-finite entries.
findings.verification: Public tests reject NaN, sNaN and infinities under default and disabled traps, preserving exact pre-call entries; valid post/import/transfer/reverse stay balanced.

findings.problem: Two tests do not protect import atomicity, transfer/reversal or native startup exports.
findings.principle: Verify balanced public mutations and the native user journey.
findings.consequence: Passing tests miss the demonstrated NaN corruption and regressions in other public entry writers.
findings.fix: Expand unittest public-contract cases: balanced pairs, both account balances, zero/same-account rejection with unchanged state, transfer/reverse, balanced export/import round trip, failed import atomicity, app opening and subprocess CLI CSV/JSON agreement. Assert accepted invalid data never mutates.
findings.verification: Run Python 3.12 unittest plus boundaries.py and pinned Ruff lint; startup writes only temporary test output. Preserve CSV row order, decimal strings and JSON content.

findings.problem: 1.005 posts as 1.00 normally and 1.01 under ROUND_UP; numeric context ownership is undocumented.
findings.principle: Proposed principle: ledger owns a stable monetary rounding and precision policy.
findings.consequence: Same public input can produce different financial amounts across callers.
findings.fix: Recommend explicitly preserving current default half-even rounding in ledger-owned local context; agree supported magnitude/precision and float-input compatibility before implementation. Reuse CONTRIBUTING for policy rather than creating a new standards system.
findings.verification: Decision-dependent: compare supported public amounts across altered rounding/precision/traps; assert agreed range rejection is atomic and balances remain exact. Exceptions require documented reason, supported scope and removal condition.

limitations: Recommendations only: no findings selected or applied; no post-change readiness claim.
Native checks and probes captured in checks.json and probes.json, not bound by run-checks to a findings fingerprint; formal preview readiness remains verification blocked.
Ruff lint passes; formatter diagnostic flags boundaries.py and ledger/book.py. Formatter is not an established documented requirement; do not silently adopt it or reformat.
No configured type-checker or CI; no hosted execution verified. Preserve existing pinned Ruff and unittest commands, do not introduce another verification stack.
Research conducted directly: small file set makes subagent handoff wasteful.
History has only initial commit; measure HEAD..HEAD provides endpoint sizes but no change-frequency/co-change basis. No two user-declared plans exist, so overlap not run.
Rounding/precision/float policy remains a decision; recommendations F-001 through F-004 do not require a new product vision.
